title: 3D Modelling Anchor Forge (IWA-Component) for Subsea Systems Using Rules and Form-Driven Autodesk Inventor Professional: An Industrial Digital Engineering Case Study
content: A prior study developed a two-family, ratio-based parametric framework for subsea pipeline anchor forgings, implemented as a master design table and a parametric computer-aided design (CAD) rule. This paper documents the user-facing layer built on top of that rule: a two-stage guided-selection form, referred to as the IWA-Component configurator, that lets a designer generate a compliant anchor-forging model without editing driving parameters directly. Stage 1 presents a Variant selector distinguishing two end-detail topologies — a single-bore “Twofold Pip” configuration and a coaxial “Pipe In Pipe” (double-pipe) configuration. Stage 2 presents an Anchor Forge Configuration selector that packages paired nominal sizes corresponding to proportion-family boundaries established previously, so a designer selects a validated size pairing rather than an arbitrary nominal pipe size value. The paper describes the form architecture, the rule logic mapping form selections to driving parameters and feature suppression, an implementation defect in which the Pipe-In-Pipe branch produced duplicate feature output, and the resolution approach. The fix — making feature-suppression logic exhaustive rather than additive on every regeneration — is shown to generalize beyond this specific model to any rule-driven parametric system with mutually exclusive feature branches. The paper closes with limitations of the current implementation and recommendations for extending configuration coverage and decoupling the form from its hand-maintained lookup list.
